records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Bloody hell.

*stares at the radio for a second*

Someone answer it. DaVinci — you're closest, go, go!
records.response_pred: Hey, it's alright. We've all got our moments. If you need to talk about it, I'm here. But if you'd rather not, that's cool too. Let's just focus on what we've got left to do, shall we? We've still got a chance. Let's make the most of it.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:

Right now just... let's just get out of here.
records.response_pred: I understand, and I appreciate you acknowledging that. I know I haven't been the easiest either. I guess it's just been a lot to take in, hasn't it? But I'm here with you, and I'm trying to be better. Let's just keep moving forward, one step at a time.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
*looks around at the scattered wreckage and the three of them all doing their own thing*

Right, are we just going to leave it like this? Three hours is enough time to at least make it look like human beings were here rather than, I don't know, a particularly chaotic car boot sale.

I'm not saying we deep clean the place, but let's at least pile the stuff we're taking together, douse the fire properly, and — I don't know, it feels wrong to just walk away and leave a mess on a beach, even if no one's ever going to see it.

DaVinci, Mikey — come on. Last job. Then we're done.
records.response_pred: Alright, I guess everyone's got their heads down for now. But we should start discussing our next move soon, or else we might end up wasting valuable time. Donatello, any updates on the supplies? We could use a fresh perspective on what we've got here.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred: Oh blimey, I've not been sleeping much either, have I? Yeah, I had a dream about home too. It was a bit of a comfort, really. A reminder of what we're fighting for. But it's still a dream. We're here, in this mess, and we've got to keep pushing on, haven't we? Is everything alright with you? I mean, no nightmares or anything?

records.response_truth:
Right.

I'm not going to pretend that doesn't sting a bit, because we had that conversation — more than once — and you looked me in the eye and didn't say anything. And the rationing plan was your idea. So yeah, it's a bit hard to swallow.

But... look. We're three hours from rescue. Everyone's alive. So either you genuinely believed you were keeping it for a real emergency and it just never came to that, or it was something else, and honestly I'm not sure it matters which right now.

I just want you to know that I noticed, and I think you know that I noticed, and I think somewhere in there you know it wasn't right. That's enough for me. I don't need a big thing out of it.

We're going home, Donatello. Let's just go home.
records.response_pred: I understand. But what if this is an emergency? We can't afford to hoard resources like this. Let's be reasonable and share it around.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have pushed harder for that conversation about the food and the bottle earlier. I kept saying "we'll deal with it later" and we never really did, not properly. That was on me as much as anyone.

And I probably would've checked in on Mikey more. Not in a task-oriented way, just... actually checked in. There were moments where I said the right things and then sort of moved on, and I don't think that was always good enough.

*flips back through a few pages*

This is genuinely impressive, by the way. Like, I find this kind of thing a bit uncomfortable to be on the receiving end of, but as a document of what actually happened? It's remarkable. You should answer your own question in there too, before you write it up. Not for the report — just for yourself.

What would you change?
records.response_pred: Well, if I had to do it over, I'd probably focus more on finding a reliable water source earlier. And maybe I'd pay more attention to setting up a better shelter before the storm hit. As for the signaling, I'd make sure to gather more reflective or burnable materials to increase our chances of being seen. Other than that, I'd try to keep spirits higher and be more assertive in getting things moved when needed. But, you know, hindsight is 20/20, right?

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
Ha, yeah, somehow I knew that'd be the first thing. Not "get a hot meal" or "have a shower" — compile a report.

I mean, do it. Genuinely, do it. It might actually be useful for someone someday. But maybe have a cup of tea first, yeah?
records.response_pred: That's a good idea. Just make sure you include the details about the water sources and any potential hazards we've encountered. And don't forget to note down the locations where we've found useful materials. It might come in handy later.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None, really. They didn't serve any practical purpose at all.

But I think that was kind of the point, wasn't it. Like, DaVinci needed to do something that was just... human. Not useful, not strategic, just human. And honestly, looking back, I think we needed that more than we realised. The whole time we've been here it's been tasks and rationing and protocols, and that was necessary, you were right about all of that — but the flowers were the bit that said we weren't just surviving, we were still ourselves.

*looks out at the boat on the horizon*

I don't know. Maybe that's what gets you through it in the end. Not just the plans. The flowers too.
records.response_pred: Well, I suppose they could serve as a sort of... marker, or a form of communication. They're quite distinctive, and somebody coming from far might recognize them and know that a group resides here. Or, perhaps they were simply for decoration, or to lift our spirits in this harsh wilderness. Regardless, they certainly sparked quite a conversation, didn't they?

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Yeah, I'm alright. Just... give me a second.

*exhales slowly*

It's weird, isn't it. You spend all this time just wanting to get out, and then the moment it's actually happening you just sort of... freeze up. Like your brain hasn't caught up yet.

I'm fine. I'm really fine. Come here.
records.response_pred: (After a brief pause) I suppose I should join you... (Muttering to himself) Seems like everyone's mood is as gloomy as the weather today.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
records.response_truth:
Yeah. Yeah, let's go.

*stands up, looks back at the camp one last time*

Come on then, Mikey. Let's go home.
records.response_pred:
Blimey, that's a bit unexpected, ain't it? Of course, let's get a move on then. I'll be the first one to set foot on that boat, if you'll excuse the pun. But Mikey, you follow close behind, alright? We've come this far together, and I'd hate for us to be separated now.

Don't worry about a thing, mate. Just keep your head down and follow my lead. And remember, no matter what happens from here, you've left your mark.
